findings.title: Regression: regenerated config_regs stores writes to reserved (RO) bits of RW registers
findings.detail: The previous config_regs (drop dce7b40) masked every write to the fields the register map declares; the regenerated one stores all 32 bits. Under the register walk, writing 0xFFFFFFFF / 0xA5A5A5A5 / 0x5A5A5A5A reads back unmasked on every RW register that has a reserved RO field: REFRESH_CONFIG (0x18, fields in bits 8:0, expected 0x1ff read 0xffffffff), CTRL_CONFIG (0x04, expected 0x1f read 0xffffff1f — the WO self-clearing bits are still handled), BIST_CONFIG (0x20, expected 0xf read 0xffffffff), BIST_ADDR_START and BIST_ADDR_END (0x24 / 0x28, 29-bit fields, expected 0x1fffffff read 0xffffffff). 15 of the 16 config_regs mismatches in paths 12 and 13 are this defect; the 16th is the previously filed status-read sampling question. VP_CSR_001 (RO field semantics: writes ignored) covers reserved fields; the gate-accepted register-map predictor caught it on the first run of the new drop, which is the closed loop working as intended.

evidence.stage: config_regs (exact) matched 87/103, was 102/103 on drop dce7b40
evidence.rtl_diff_hint: confirmed at source: dce7b40 config_regs.sv line 176 wrote reg_refresh_config[3:0], [7:4], [8] per field; b4d6f45 line 230 writes reg_refresh_config[7:0] / [15:8] / ... per byte lane under csr_sel_i, so reserved bits 31:9 take the written value. The byte-lane structure is an improvement (the old RTL ignored csr_sel_i); the field mask was lost in the rewrite.
